question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\0&k&4\\2&1&5\end{bmatrix}$, the cofactors $A_{12}$ and $A_{21}$ are equal. Determine $k$.
explanation:
Step 1: Find $A_{12}$
Deleting the first row and second column gives $$M_{12}=\begin{vmatrix}0&4\\2&5\end{vmatrix}=-8$$ Since $1+2$ is odd, $$A_{12}=-M_{12}=8$$
Step 2: Find $A_{21}$
Deleting the second row and first column gives $$M_{21}=\begin{vmatrix}2&3\\1&5\end{vmatrix}=10-3=7$$ Since $2+1$ is odd, $$A_{21}=-M_{21}=-7$$
Step 3: Compare the cofactors
Both values are independent of $k$, and $8\ne-7$.
Step 4: Conclude
Therefore, no value of $k$ can make $A_{12}=A_{21}$.

options.B: No value of $k$ satisfies the condition.
